title: Add a phone list preview route for the SMS review step
body: The SMS review step shows how many people a list will reach only after the build finishes, so an official who wants to narrow a list has to build it, wait, and start over. This adds `POST /p2p/phone-list/preview`, which runs the same resolution the build does (saved filter, opt-out scrub, the 200,000 cap, the geo-targetable address check) and returns the recipient count and what the list drops, without creating a build row or calling Peerly. The webapp change to call it follows separately.
author: delegate-eval

+  // Read-only: resolves the list and returns its counts without creating a
+  // build row or touching Peerly.
+  @Post('phone-list/preview')
+  @UseCampaign()
+  async previewPhoneList(
+    @ReqCampaign() campaign: Campaign,
+    @Body() request: P2pPhoneListPreviewRequestSchema,
+  ): Promise<P2pPhoneListPreviewResponseSchema> {
+    try {
+      return await this.p2pPhoneListUploadService.previewPhoneList(
+        campaign,
+        request,
+      )
+    } catch (error) {
+      if (error instanceof HttpException) {
+        throw error
+      }
+      this.logger.error({ error }, 'Failed to preview phone list')
+      throw new BadGatewayException('Failed to preview phone list.')
+    }
+  }
+

+import { createZodDto } from 'nestjs-zod'
+import { z } from 'zod'
+import { p2pPhoneListRequestSchema } from './p2pPhoneListRequest.schema'
+
+// The build request without the list name: a preview builds nothing, so
+// there is nothing to name.
+export class P2pPhoneListPreviewRequestSchema extends createZodDto(
+  p2pPhoneListRequestSchema.omit({ name: true }),
+) {}
+
+export class P2pPhoneListPreviewResponseSchema extends createZodDto(
+  z.object({
+    recipientCount: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
+    excludedDuplicatePhoneCount: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
+    excludedIncompleteAddressCount: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
+  }),
+) {}

+import { useTestService } from '@/test-service'
+import { ElectionsService } from '@/elections/services/elections.service'
+import { FeaturesService } from '@/features/services/features.service'
+import { VoterQueryService } from '@/peopleDb/services/voterQuery.service'

+
+const service = useTestService()
+
+const WIN_SLUG = 'campaign-p2p-preview'
+const ORG_SLUG_HEADER = 'X-Organization-Slug'
+const DISTRICT_ID = '20000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'
+
+const seedWinCampaign = async () => {
+  await service.prisma.organization.create({
+    data: {
+      slug: WIN_SLUG,
+      ownerId: service.user.id,
+      overrideDistrictId: DISTRICT_ID,
+    },
+  })
+  const campaign = await service.prisma.campaign.create({
+    data: {
+      userId: service.user.id,
+      slug: `${WIN_SLUG}-campaign`,
+      organizationSlug: WIN_SLUG,
+      isPro: true,
+    },
+  })
+  await service.prisma.tcrCompliance.create({
+    data: {
+      campaignId: campaign.id,
+      ein: '12-3456789',
+      postalAddress: '123 Main St',
+      committeeName: 'Test Committee',
+      websiteDomain: 'example.com',
+      filingUrl: 'https://example.com/filing',
+      phone: '5551234567',
+      email: 'test@example.com',
+      officeLevel: OfficeLevel.state,
+      peerlyIdentityId: 'peerly-identity-1',
+    },
+  })
+  return campaign
+}
+
+const personPayload = (overrides: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => ({
+  id: '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001',
+  firstName: 'Jane',
+  lastName: 'Doe',
+  cellPhone: '5551234567',
+  address: { city: 'Springfield', state: 'CA', zip: '90210' },
+  ...overrides,
+})
+
+const stubPeopleApi = (
+  people: Record<string, unknown>[],
+  totalResults = people.length,
+) =>
+  vi.spyOn(service.app.get(VoterQueryService), 'findPeople').mockResolvedValue({
+    people,
+    pagination: {
+      totalResults,
+      currentPage: 1,
+      pageSize: people.length,
+      totalPages: 1,
+      hasNextPage: false,
+      hasPreviousPage: false,
+    },
+  } as never)
+
+const preview = (body: Record<string, unknown> = {}) =>
+  service.client.post('/v1/p2p/phone-list/preview', body, {
+    headers: { [ORG_SLUG_HEADER]: WIN_SLUG },
+  })
+
+describe('POST /v1/p2p/phone-list/preview', () => {
+  beforeEach(() => {
+    vi.spyOn(
+      service.app.get(FeaturesService),
+      'isFeatureEnabled',
+    ).mockResolvedValue(false)
+    vi.spyOn(
+      service.app.get(ElectionsService),
+      'getDistrict',
+    ).mockResolvedValue({
+      id: DISTRICT_ID,
+      state: 'CA',
+      L2DistrictType: 'County',
+      L2DistrictName: 'Test County',
+      projectedTurnout: null,
+    } as never)
+  })
+
+  it('counts the recipients and what the list drops, without building', async () => {
+    await seedWinCampaign()
+    stubPeopleApi([
+      personPayload(),
+      personPayload({
+        id: '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002',
+        cellPhone: '5551234567',
+      }),
+      personPayload({
+        id: '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003',
+        cellPhone: '5559876543',
+        address: { city: 'Springfield', state: 'CA', zip: null },
+      }),
+      personPayload({
+        id: '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000004',
+        cellPhone: '5550001111',
+      }),
+    ])
+    const upload = vi.spyOn(
+      service.app.get(PeerlyPhoneListService),
+      'uploadPhoneList',
+    )
+
+    const result = await preview()
+
+    expect(result.status).toBe(201)
+    expect(result.data).toEqual({
+      recipientCount: 2,
+      excludedDuplicatePhoneCount: 1,
+      excludedIncompleteAddressCount: 1,
+    })
+    expect(upload).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+    expect(await service.prisma.peerlyPhoneList.count()).toBe(0)
+  })
+
+  it('refuses a list over the recipient cap', async () => {
+    await seedWinCampaign()
+    const findPeople = stubPeopleApi([personPayload()], 200_001)
+
+    const result = await preview()
+
+    expect(result.status).toBe(400)
+    expect(result.data.message).toMatch(/This list reaches over 200,000/)
+    expect(findPeople).toHaveBeenCalledOnce()
+  })
+
+  it('rejects a voterFileFilterId owned by another organization', async () => {
+    await seedWinCampaign()
+    await service.prisma.organization.create({
+      data: { slug: 'other-org-preview', ownerId: service.user.id },
+    })
+    const foreignFilter = await service.prisma.voterFileFilter.create({
+      data: { organizationSlug: 'other-org-preview', name: 'Not yours' },
+    })
+    const findPeople = stubPeopleApi([personPayload()])
+
+    const result = await preview({ voterFileFilterId: foreignFilter.id })
+
+    expect(result.status).toBe(400)
+    expect(findPeople).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+})
diff --git a/packages/gp-api/src/vendors/peerly/services/p2pPhoneListUpload.service.ts b/packages/gp-api/src/vendors/peerly/services/p2pPhoneListUpload.service.ts

+++ b/packages/gp-api/src/vendors/peerly/services/p2pPhoneListUpload.service.ts
@@ -598,6 +598,72 @@ export class P2pPhoneListUploadService {
     )
   }
 
+  // The counts the review step shows before the official commits to a list:
+  // who the list would reach, and who it would drop for a shared phone or an
+  // address Peerly can't geo-target. Runs the same resolution as the build
+  // (same filter, same opt-out scrub, same cap) and uploads nothing, so the
+  // number shown is the number the build produces.
+  async previewPhoneList(
+    campaign: Campaign,
+    filterInput: P2pPhoneListFilterInput,
+  ): Promise<{
+    recipientCount: number
+    excludedDuplicatePhoneCount: number
+    excludedIncompleteAddressCount: number
+  }> {
+    const organization = await this.organizationsService.findFirst({
+      where: { slug: campaign.organizationSlug },
+    })
+    if (!organization) {
+      throw new BadRequestException('Organization not found for campaign')
+    }
+    const resolvedFilterInput = await this.resolveFilterInput(
+      filterInput,
+      campaign.organizationSlug,
+    )
+    if (resolvedFilterInput === null) {
+      throw new BadRequestException('Voter file filter not found')
+    }
+    const excludePersonIds = await this.resolveOptOutScrub(
+      campaign.organizationSlug,
+    )
+
+    let excludedIncompleteAddressCount = 0
+    const audience = resolveFilterAudience(this.contactsService, {
+      filterInput: resolvedFilterInput,
+      organization,
+      dataset: await this.contactsService.resolvePeopleDataset(organization),
+      excludePersonIds,
+      pageSize: SEGMENT_PAGE_SIZE,
+      maxRecipients: MAX_PHONE_LIST_RECIPIENTS,
+      isEligible: (person) => {
+        if (hasGeoTargetableAddress(person)) return true
+        excludedIncompleteAddressCount += 1
+        return false
+      },
+      limitExceededMessage:
+        `This list reaches over ` +
+        `${MAX_PHONE_LIST_RECIPIENTS.toLocaleString('en-US')} people, which ` +
+        `is more than one text campaign can send to. Narrow your filters ` +
+        `and try again.`,
+    })
+
+    // The duplicate count is the generator's return value, which
+    // `for await...of` discards, so drive it by hand.
+    let recipientCount = 0
+    let next = await audience.next()
+    while (!next.done) {
+      recipientCount += 1
+      next = await audience.next()
+    }
+
+    return {
+      recipientCount,
+      excludedDuplicatePhoneCount: next.value.excludedDuplicatePhoneCount,
+      excludedIncompleteAddressCount,
+    }
+  }
+
   // Resolves a persisted voterFileFilterId into the full saved-segment
   // criteria, inline fields overriding — mirroring how getListDetail resolves
   // a persisted filter. Without this the id would be captured while the list
diff --git a/packages/gp-api/src/voters/AGENTS.md b/packages/gp-api/src/voters/AGENTS.md
index 1f37f7473b..b3f4e0c10e 100644
--- a/packages/gp-api/src/voters/AGENTS.md
+++ b/packages/gp-api/src/voters/AGENTS.md
@@ -29,5 +29,6 @@ This module does not store the voter file itself. We persist filters, derived co
 - **The legacy voter datastore is retired** (ENG-5032). `GET /voters/voter-file` (the outreach/task-flow audience download and count — `downloadVoterList.util.ts` / `RecordCount` in gp-webapp) resolves through `ContactsService.countVoterFilePeople` / `downloadVoterFilePeople` → the `src/peopleDb` query/download services — mapping the legacy underscore filters and per-type population rules in `voterFile/util/voterFilePeopleFilter.util.ts` (mirrors `segmentsToFiltersMap.const.ts`). Those two `ContactsService` methods are deliberately NOT pro-gated — the endpoint never was; `CanDownloadVoterFileGuard` owns access. The CSV is a curated ~76-column subset with friendly headers (`DOWNLOAD_COLUMNS` in `src/peopleDb/voter.select.ts`, ENG-10766, widened in DATA-2281) — not the raw L2 columns, and not the voter engine's full internal projection either.
 - `VotersModule` imports `OutreachModule` (one-way). If you find yourself wanting `OutreachModule` to import voters too, route the dependency through an existing service instead — adding a back-edge will require `forwardRef` and is a smell.
 - **The SMS/Peerly phone-list path resolves through `ContactsService.findContactsForFilter`** (ENG-10728) — the same activityConditions/supportStatus/search resolution engine list/count/download use — paged (`SEGMENT_PAGE_SIZE` 1000, 200k cap) with `hasCellPhone: true` forced (`src/vendors/peerly/services/p2pPhoneListUpload.service.ts`). `peerly/utils/audienceMapping.util.ts` is deleted; don't resurrect it for new Peerly filter mapping.
+- **`POST /p2p/phone-list/preview` counts a list without building it.** Same body as the build minus `name`; it runs the build's resolution (`P2pPhoneListUploadService.previewPhoneList`: filter, opt-out scrub, cap, geo-targetable address) and returns `recipientCount` plus the duplicate-phone and incomplete-address drops. No `PeerlyPhoneList` row, no Peerly call.
 - **Every uploaded Peerly phone list is captured — the row exists before the token does.** `POST /p2p/phone-list` creates the `PeerlyPhoneList` row FIRST (`PeerlyPhoneListCaptureService.createQueuedBuild`, `buildStatus: queued`, no token, plus a `requestSnapshot` of the validated body), then builds/uploads against that same row's id (`buildId`) as the handle. `recordUpload` UPDATES that row (token, the two exclusion counts, `buildStatus: processing`) and inserts one `PeerlyPhoneListRecipient` row per CSV line — `(personId, phone)` — in a single transaction, only after the Peerly upload itself succeeds; it never inserts a second row. If the build throws anywhere (empty audience, Peerly error, the Pro-access check inside `ContactsService`), `markBuildFailed` parks the row `buildStatus: failed` with a short `buildError` before the same exception rethrows to the caller — a build never leaves a `queued`/`building` orphan. The POST response carries both `token` (`null` on the async path until the build reaches Peerly) and `buildId`. Either status route — the original `GET /p2p/phone-list/:token/status` or the additive `GET /p2p/phone-list/build/:buildId/status` (ownership-checked on `campaignId` the same way) — shares one resolution path (`P2pController.resolveListStatus`) that polls Peerly and, once ACTIVE, only stamps `peerlyListId`/`buildStatus: ready` once `leads_loaded` has STABILIZED (`PeerlyPhoneListCaptureService.isLeadsLoadedStable`): either it already equals Peerly's `leads_supplied` (a small list, which still stabilizes on the very first read) or it reads the same value across two consecutive polls (`PeerlyPhoneList.lastSeenLeadsLoaded`). A still-climbing large list gets a 202 instead of a premature `ready`. The ready transition (this route or the server finisher) logs `Peerly phone list ready` with Peerly's per-reason drop counts (`peerlyScrubCounts`: duplicate, malformed, invalid, the DNC buckets, cell-suppressed). Read it when `leads_loaded` is far under what we uploaded: Florida lists lose 40-55% there while other states lose about 1% (ENG-11484), and nothing else records why. `peerlyListId` equals `Outreach.phoneListId`, which downstream materialization/inbound-mapping tasks use to find the capture row.
   **The build itself moves off the request onto the queue behind the managed Amplitude flag `win_sms_hold_billing`** (evaluated per-user at the upload request via `FeaturesService`; off — synchronous, unchanged; the async build is the whole reason hold-billing exists, so the two ship as one flag). On: the POST only creates the `queued` row and enqueues `QueueType.P2P_PHONE_LIST_BUILD` (`{ buildId }`), returning `{ buildId, token: null }` immediately; `P2pPhoneListUploadService.handleQueuedBuild` does the rest (TCR compliance, organization, filter resolution, opt-out scrub, CSV, Peerly upload, `recordUpload`) off a single-owner CAS claim (`queued -> building`, count 0 = another delivery already owns it or it advanced — ack). The Peerly token is stamped (`stampBuildToken`) the moment Peerly accepts the upload, BEFORE the slower recipients write, so a redelivery that finds a token already on the row skips the upload entirely rather than ever sending the same list to Peerly twice. A `building` row stuck past `P2P_PHONE_LIST_BUILD_STALE_MINUTES` is reclaimed by a `@Cron` sweep (per-record CAS, no whole-job lock — same reasoning as `OutreachRobocallStagingService`'s stale-staging reclaim) back to `queued` and re-enqueued, or parked `failed` after `P2P_PHONE_LIST_BUILD_MAX_ATTEMPTS`. The queued build has no request deadline, so it skips the interactive path's page-1 preflight cap (`skipPreflightCap`) — see `audienceResolution.util.ts`.
